questions.explanation: Errors here usually come from swapping in a claim the position rejects. A false dilemma presents only two options when others exist. This is the position defended by Aristotle. The claim that a false dilemma correctly lists all possible options is a common mistake about the view, often described as "misreads false dilemma as exhaustive". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: real dilemmas do exist. A careful reader separates the actual doctrine from the frequent misreading.
